questions.stem: How does the reactivity of halogens change going down Group 7?
questions.explanation: Reactivity decreases going down Group 7. This is because atoms get larger with more shielding, making it harder for the nucleus to attract an incoming electron. Fluorine is the most reactive halogen, and iodine is the least reactive of the commonly studied ones.

questions.stem: What happens when chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution?

options.text: The solution turns orange as chlorine displaces bromine

questions.explanation: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces bromine from potassium bromide solution. The solution turns orange as free bromine is released: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂. A more reactive halogen always displaces a less reactive one.
